evidence.appropriate: round 3: the K reads first, then the stone at its junction that the arm and leg lean on; the idea takes one sentence, not a paragraph; heavy and plain (Everyman)
evidence.distinctive: no competitor uses a K and there is no tile (unlike FreshBooks and Bonsai), but a heavy K is a common letterform; the junction stone is the only ownable detail and it closes below 48 px
evidence.simple: one letter and one stone, 36 anchors; 'a K with a stone at its heart'
evidence.legible: the K reads at 16 px (the favicon closes the joints into a plain K); the joints read from 48 px; the stone never turns the K into another letter (Kia test)
evidence.adaptable: one colour and reversed both hold; the icon is the K; motion: the stone slides in from the jaw and the letter locks; at 16 px it is a plain K
evidence.timeless: no avoid-list trend; a mono-initial app icon is a 'use carefully' item, with its reason in strategy.md section 8
evidence.universal: mirrored reads as a reversed K, as any letter does; rotated 90 shows the construction, an arch with its keystone at the crown; at 64 to 128 px the trapezoid inside the K can read as a loudspeaker
evidence.clear: description searches ('letter K logo with keystone wedge', 'K monogram') found generic K monograms and K-with-a-key stock logos, nothing with a keystone at the junction
evidence.congruent: heavy, grotesk and low complexity match; shape 0.4 matches (curved arm and leg on a straight stem); symmetry (target 0.85), frame (framed) and dynamism (0.2) miss: a K is asymmetric, open and leans; the hard K suits the name's sound
evidence.system: horizontal, stacked, symbol, compact, small and favicon all build; the favicon is a plain K; rationale draft in critique.md
